# Playbook: start
Use when: start or continue work on one activity

How to run this playbook:
- Follow steps in order. CALL sends the shown arguments; RUN executes a command. FOR EACH repeats its indented lines.
- Replace `<input:x>` from You need, `<saved:x>` from SAVE, `<each:x>` from the current item. Whole placeholders retain their JSON type, including numbers, arrays, objects and null; embedded ones are text. Never invent concurrency tokens. `result` is the last call's response.
- IF tests a condition; go to step N jumps forward; go to Answer ends execution.
- ASK waits for the user's answer unless that exact action is already authorized. STOP ends calls and puts its message in Next. Owner-only actions require the owner's order.
- VERIFY must pass before reporting success. Fill the Answer block in the user's language; copy IDs exactly. Secrets never enter the reply.

## You need
| Input | Where it comes from | If missing |
|---|---|---|
| projectId | the user, or `recommendation.projectId` of `recommend_next_activity` | STOP. Say: "Which LPM project? (id or name)" |
| issueId | the user, `.lpm-activity`, or `recommendation.issueId` | STOP. Say: "Which LPM activity should I start? (id or title)" |
| repo | the folder of the git repository you will change | "none" (no code work) |
| deploying | "yes" when the user said a deploy or upload runs from that folder | "no" |

## Steps
Every CALL or RUN with no error line: IF it returns an error → STOP. Say: "<tool or command> failed: <error text>. Nothing was changed."
1. CALL `get_issue` {"projectId":"<input:projectId>","issueId":"<input:issueId>"} [A]
   IF the call returns an error → STOP. Say: "<input:issueId> was not found in <input:projectId>: <error text>. Which activity? (id or title)"
   SAVE: title = result.title; status = result.status; was = result.status; description = result.description; workspaceId = result.workspaceId
   IF result.blockerContext.status == "active" → STOP. This belongs to skill `lpm-unblock-work`. Say: "<input:issueId> has an active blocker: <result.blockerContext.content>."
2. CALL `list_comments` {"projectId":"<input:projectId>","issueId":"<input:issueId>"} [A]
   SAVE: criteria = the list lines of <saved:description> plus comment lines that start with "Acceptance", "Critério", "Pending" or "Pendente"
3. IF <saved:status> == "in-progress" → go to step 6.
   IF <saved:status> is "backlog" or "todo" → go to step 5.
4. ASK: "<input:issueId> is <saved:status>. Reopen it (set in-progress)? (yes/no)" — continue only if the user says yes; otherwise STOP.
5. CALL `update_issue` {"projectId":"<input:projectId>","issueId":"<input:issueId>","status":"in-progress"} [A]
   VERIFY: CALL `get_issue` {"projectId":"<input:projectId>","issueId":"<input:issueId>"} [A]
   IF the call returns an error or result.status != "in-progress" → STOP. Say: "<input:issueId> is still <result.status>; the status did not change."
   SAVE: status = result.status
6. IF <input:repo> is "none" → go to Answer.
   IF <input:deploying> is "yes" → STOP. Say: "A deploy runs from <input:repo>. Create a git worktree (git worktree add <path> -b <branch>) and give me its folder."
7. CALL `get_skills_context` {"projectId":"<input:projectId>"} [A]
   IF the call returns an error or null → SAVE: rules = "none"; go to step 8.
   SAVE: rules = result.instructions and result.toolingNotes
8. RUN `git -C <input:repo> status --short`
   SAVE: dirty = the paths it lists (files changed before you started; never commit them as yours)
9. SAVE: checks = the test, lint and check commands that the repository's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or CONTRIBUTING.md name (read the files that exist; in the lpm repository read AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md)

## Answer (reply with exactly this block, filled in; write nothing before or after it)
```text
Scope: <saved:workspaceId>/<input:projectId>/<input:issueId> <saved:title>
Done: <status <saved:was> → in-progress | no status change>; <coding rules read | no coding rules>; status <saved:status>
Evidence: none yet
Pending: <each line of <saved:criteria> | no acceptance criteria written yet>
Next: <the ASK or STOP text that ended the run | implement it, run <saved:checks>, then run playbook commit-and-progress>
```
status: backlog | todo | in-progress | done | canceled, from your last get_issue. Never claim a status change that step 5's VERIFY did not show.
